overview: The Tu'i Tonga chiefly tradition is visible in the monumental landscapes of Tongatapu and in remembered connections across the Pacific. Oral histories and archaeological evidence need distinct date labels; the map's broad interval cannot resolve every shift in chiefly authority.

items.text: Ha'amonga a Maui consists of upright coral-limestone slabs supporting a lintel. Recorded tradition associates the monument with Tu'itatui and a royal compound.
Lapaha's langi are raised earth burial platforms faced with carefully fitted stone slabs. Their construction required coordinated specialist labour.
Recorded accounts connect the move to Lapaha with sheltered anchorage for double-hulled canoes used on long voyages. This is a tradition reported in the nomination, not a dated engineering survey.
A solar-calendar interpretation of Ha'amonga has been proposed. The nomination itself notes that this idea may be modern, so its original astronomical purpose remains uncertain.
Burial practices and care of the langi remain living traditions. Tongan communities also sustain cloth-making and extended-family obligations across the diaspora.
